items.body:
## Problem

`WorldClient::manifest_state` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:961-995`, on
`origin/main` 075b2de904) reads the two fields of the `world_state`
reply with opposite strictness:

```rust
Some("world_state") => Ok((
    reply["seed"].as_u64(),                                   // :978
    serde_json::from_value(reply["schedules"].clone())
        .context("host sent a malformed schedule map")?,      // :979-980
)),
```

`schedules` is decoded strictly and a malformed map errors. `seed` is
read with a bare `as_u64()`: a **present but mistyped** seed — `"42"`,
`-1`, `1.5`, `{}` — silently becomes `None`, indistinguishable from
the one legitimate `None` case, a capability-only read where the host
deliberately hides the seed (#240; `world_session/tests.rs:685`
"schedule_and_world_state_frames_round_trip_and_hide_the_seed").

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real `id` crate, scripted host)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-policy-wt/pkgs/id/tests/probe_policy_reply.rs`,
test `probe_manifest_state_seed_shapes`:

- CONTROL `{"type":"world_state","seed":42,"schedules":{"a":1}}` →
  `Ok((Some(42), {"a":1}))`.
- CONTROL no `seed` field (capability-only shape) → `Ok((None, {}))`
  — the legitimate `None`.
- CASES seed `"42"` / `-1` / `1.5` / `{}` → all `Ok((None, {}))`,
  identical to the legitimate hidden-seed result.
- ORACLE mistyped `schedules` (`{"a":"x"}`) → `Err`, proving the
  sibling field in the same reply is validated.

## Why it matters

The consumer is world-manifest capture
(`commands/world.rs:1145`, `capture_world_state`): it takes the
returned seed into `WorldState { seed: seed.unwrap_or(0), .. }`, the
state that `id world apply`/diff reconciles against. An admin read
whose seed arrived mistyped is silently downgraded to the
capability-only shape and then baked in as **seed 0** — a fabricated
install seed in the captured manifest, with no error anywhere. The
reply's own contract already distinguishes the two cases (field absent
= hidden; field present = the seed); the client just has to check
presence before type, the way the schedules arm checks its type.

## Acceptance criteria

- `manifest_state` errors when the `seed` field is present but not a
  `u64` (string, negative, float, object, array, bool), with an error
  naming the malformed seed; a genuinely absent seed still returns
  `None` for capability-only reads.
- Regression tests with a scripted host covering: numeric seed,
  absent seed, and each mistyped-seed shape; mistyped `schedules`
  continues to error.
- No change to the host side or to the #240 seed-hiding behavior.

items.body:
# id(world_net): create_world reads a missing or mistyped `created` flag as Ok(false) — a malformed `world_created` reply reports "exists" for a world that may not exist

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ origin/main 075b2de904)

`WorldClient::create_world` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:1226`) checks only that the reply frame's `type` is `"world_created"`, then reads the outcome flag with a silent default:

- `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:1245` — `Ok(reply["created"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false))`

`false` is a real, meaningful answer here: the host (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs:977-986`) replies `ServerFrame::WorldCreated { world, created }` where `created: false` means the world already existed. So a `world_created` reply whose `created` field is missing or mistyped (host bug, version skew, hostile host) is indistinguishable from "already exists" — the client reports `Ok(false)` and never errors.

The sole caller trusts the bool directly:

- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:772-777` (`id world create`): `println!("{}", if result? { "created" } else { "exists" })` and exits `Ok(())` — a malformed reply prints `exists` and exits 0, telling the operator the world is there when the reply never actually said so.

Sibling `WorldClient` methods refuse exactly this shape instead of defaulting: `set_isolation` requires the field with `.context("host sent no isolation")` (`world_net.rs:1155-1158`), `info_details` requires `world_id`/`current_sequence` with context errors (`:1473-1478`), `set_schedule`/`cancel_schedule` parse via `from_value` with "host sent a malformed schedule map" (`:909`/`:943`), and `manifest_state` does the same (`:979`).

## Reproduction (probe, laptop)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-world-reply-defaults` (verbatim extraction of the reply tail `world_net.rs:1237-1245`; only the transport is replaced by passing the reply `Value` in):

- control `{"type":"world_created","world":"arena","created":true}` -> `Ok(true)`
- control `{"type":"world_created","world":"arena","created":false}` -> `Ok(false)` (legitimate "exists")
- MISSING `created` (`{"type":"world_created","world":"arena"}`) -> `Ok(false)` — silently reads as "exists"
- MISTYPED `created` (`"created":"true"`) -> `Ok(false)` — silently reads as "exists"

PROBE PASS (cargo run --offline, laptop). Note the same probe run also reproduced the `policy_request` null/verbatim behavior — that half is already tracked as #6625 and is NOT part of this issue.

## Why it matters

`id world create` is how an operator provisions a world. Today a garbled success reply produces a confident, wrong answer — "exists", exit 0 — for a world whose creation was never confirmed. The operator (or a script checking the output) proceeds as if the world is ready; the failure surfaces later, elsewhere, with no trace back to the bad reply. This is the same silent-default family as #6620 (compile) and #6621 (read_worlds), in a distinct method with a distinct user-visible lie.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorldClient::create_world` rejects a `world_created` reply whose `created` field is missing or not a bool, with an error in the existing style (e.g. "host sent no created flag" / "host sent a malformed world_created reply")
- [ ] Well-formed replies still return `Ok(true)` (newly created) and `Ok(false)` (already existed) unchanged; the refusal path (non-`world_created` type) still surfaces the host's message
- [ ] A regression test feeds `create_world` (or its reply extraction) the missing/mistyped shapes and asserts Err; the two control shapes assert Ok(true)/Ok(false)
- [ ] `cargo test -p id world_net` (laptop or CI) green, including the existing create-world-over-iroh tests (`world_session/tests.rs:1724-1770` region)

Distinct from: #6620 (compile reply defaults), #6621 (read_worlds reply drops), #6624 (caps/update_caps report), #6625 (policy_request policy) — same family, different method and consequence. The typed server side is `ServerFrame::WorldCreated { world, created }` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs:981-984`); only the client extraction is unchecked.

items.body:
## Problem

`WorldClient::info_details` in `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs` (reply handling at :1473 on main `075b2de904`) reads the `module_info` reply's active module hash with a bare optional coercion:

```rust
let active_module_hash = reply["active_module_hash"].as_str().map(str::to_owned);
```

`as_str()` returns `None` for **every** non-string value, so a present-but-mistyped `active_module_hash` (number, bool, array, object) is silently read as `None` — the exact value that legitimately means "this world has no installed module". The host's `ServerFrame::ModuleInfo` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs:330-336`) always serializes this field as either a string or `null`, so a non-string, non-null value can only be corruption, a version-skewed host, or a hostile/buggy peer — and the client should say so instead of inventing "no module".

The same reply is otherwise strict, which is the in-function oracle:

- `world_id` missing/mistyped → error (`"host omitted world id"`, :1469-1472)
- `current_sequence` missing/mistyped → error (`"host omitted sequence"`, :1474-1476)
- a non-null `active_module_provenance` that fails to decode → error (`"host sent invalid module provenance"`, :1477-1482)

Only the hash field collapses malformed → absent.

## Why it matters

Consumers trust `None` as a factual statement about the world:

- `id world download` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:214-216`) turns the coerced `None` into the operator-facing claim "world has no installed module to download" — wrong diagnosis for a world that does have a module, sending debugging in the wrong direction.
- `capture_world_state` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:1148`) bakes `module_hash: info.active_module_hash` into the captured `WorldState` manifest — a mistyped reply is recorded as a manifest with **no module**, the same class of fabricated capture state as the manifest seed issue (#6626, different field/function).
- `id world info` JSON output (`commands/world.rs:665`) prints `"active_module_hash": null`, indistinguishable from a genuinely module-less world.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop against main `075b2de904`, real `id` crate with a scripted iroh host (`~/git/fleet/probe-compile-wt/pkgs/id/tests/probe_info_reply.rs`, test `probe_info_reply_shapes`):

- control, string hash `"abc123"` → `Ok(Some("abc123"))`
- control, `null` hash → `Ok(None)` (the legitimate no-module case)
- mistyped hash `123` / `true` / `["abc"]` / `{"h":"abc"}` → all `Ok(None)` — silently conflated with no-module
- oracle in the same reply: mistyped non-null `active_module_provenance: 123` → `Err("host sent invalid module provenance")`

Dedup: `gh search issues` for `active_module_hash` / `info_details` / `module_info` in this repo returns no issue covering `info_details` reply validation. Neighbours are distinct functions/fields: #6620 (`compile()` reply defaults), #6621 (`read_worlds_reply` entries), #6624 (`caps()` report), #6625 (`policy_request` reply), #6626 (`manifest_state` seed), #6632 (`create_world` flag).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `info_details` errors when `active_module_hash` is present and neither a string nor `null`, with an error naming the malformed field.
- [ ] A string hash still returns `Some(hash)`; `null` (and a genuinely absent field, for older hosts) still returns `None`.
- [ ] Regression tests with a scripted host (or equivalent) covering: string, null, absent, and at least number/object mistyped shapes.
- [ ] No host-side change; `ServerFrame::ModuleInfo` serialization is unchanged.

items.body:
## Phase 4 of #6669 — closing reply inventory: disposition every WorldClient reply extraction against the validated-reply contract

Design #6669 (a reply is not its defaults — one validated-reply contract for the WorldClient) states the contract in `files/designs/code-worldnet-reply-validation.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace:

1. A field that constitutes the answer is required and typed — missing/mistyped is a malformed-reply error naming the field; success fields are never defaulted.
2. Optional means absent-or-null, never mistyped (the #6633 shape).
3. Typed payloads are decoded at extraction, not cloned (validate-then-return).
4. A list reply's entries are part of the answer — a malformed entry fails the listing.
5. Extraction lives in `WorldClient`, never in callers.

Phases 1–3 are the adopted origins #6620/#6632/#6647, #6624/#6636/#6625, and #6621/#6626/#6641. This phase is the closing inventory, **gated on Phases 1–3 landing** (keep `status/blocked` until they do).

### Scope

- Inventory every public `WorldClient` method in `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs` and disposition its reply extraction against the contract with file:line evidence: conforms / covered by a filed phase / deliberately optional under rule 2 (named) / newly filed as a follow-up (linked here).
- Land the contract statement (the five rules, in their final as-built form) in the `world_net.rs` module documentation.
- Required dispositions:
  - (a) `set_execution_profile`'s whole-frame return — the remaining leg of #6635: extract-or-keep, with the reason recorded.
  - (b) Verify #6633 and #6635 close against the contract as recorded on #6669 (their fixes landed in snapshot 4ecb3510c during the design window); post the evidence on each.
  - (c) The caller-side duplicate `CapsReport` decodes at `commands/world.rs:1119-1121` and `:1231-1233` — keep as defence-in-depth or remove now that Phase 2 validates at extraction, with the reason recorded.
  - (d) Frame fields of `record_pages` and the module-download path beyond #6622's cursor scope (that design owns cursors; field shapes are this contract's).
  - (e) The `inject_json` test-target breakage (#6640/#6643) as a cross-reference only — a test-harness defect, not a reply-contract phase; confirm the phases' tests do not depend on it or name the dependency.
  - (f) Whether the per-origin rogue-host probe harnesses should consolidate into one shared scripted-host fixture in the crate's tests — disposition from the phases' as-built tests.
  - (g) Any direct host-frame reader outside `world_net.rs` (scope check only; fixture parsing at `world_fixture.rs:592-595` is already strict).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory table posted on this issue (or in the module docs) covering every public `WorldClient` method, each with a disposition and evidence.
- [ ] Contract statement present in the `world_net.rs` module documentation matching the as-built rules.
- [ ] Dispositions (a)–(g) each recorded with their outcome; any newly found lax extraction is filed as a linked follow-up, not silently fixed inside this audit or silently dropped.
- [ ] #6633/#6635 closure evidence posted (disposition (b)).

---

- **Gating:** Phases 1–3 of #6669 (#6620/#6632/#6647, #6624/#6636/#6625, #6621/#6626/#6641) must land first; this issue carries `status/blocked` until they do.

items.body:
# id(world_net): caps() and update_caps() never validate the host's capability report — a missing or malformed `report` reads as Ok(null), so an admin grant/revoke reports success with no report

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ origin/main 075b2de904)

`WorldClient::caps` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:791`) and `WorldClient::update_caps` (`:817`) check only that the reply frame's `type` is `"caps"`, then return the report field unchecked:

- `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:809` — `Ok(reply["report"].clone())` (caps)
- `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:842` — `Ok(reply["report"].clone())` (update_caps)

serde_json indexing a missing key yields `Value::Null`, and a present-but-mistyped report is cloned verbatim. Neither function ever parses the report as the typed `CapsReport` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:1426`: `granted`/`requested`/`missing`/`usage`/`policy`/`catalog`, with `#[serde(default)]` only on `ceiling`/`effective`/`view_failures`).

The strict oracle already exists in-tree, twice:

- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:1119-1121` and `:1231-1233` take the same `caps()` result and run `serde_json::from_value::<CapsReport>(...)` with `.context("host returned a malformed capability report")` — those callers reject exactly what `caps()` itself accepts.
- Sibling `WorldClient` methods validate their payloads the same way: `set_schedule`/`cancel_schedule` (`world_net.rs:909`/`:943`, "host sent a malformed schedule map"), `manifest_state` (`:979`), `metrics` (`:1444`, "host sent invalid metrics"), and `install_wasm` checks the returned hash against the uploaded module's hash (`:1401-1408`).

But other callers trust the `Value` directly:

- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:301-320` (`id world caps`): the `update_caps` result is pretty-printed and the command exits `Ok(())` — a malformed reply prints `null` and reports a successful grant/revoke.
- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:658` (world profile): the `caps()` result is embedded into the profile JSON as `"caps": <value>` — a malformed reply silently becomes `"caps": null` in an otherwise successful profile.

## Reproduction (probe, laptop)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-caps-report` (verbatim extraction from `world_net.rs:801-809`, identical in `update_caps`; `CapsReport`/`CapUsage` copied verbatim from id-core; oracle = the `from_value::<CapsReport>` check from `commands/world.rs:1120`):

- control-valid: `caps()=Ok(<report>)`, oracle Ok
- control-refusal (`type:"error"`): `caps()=Err(<host message>)`
- 8 malformed shapes — missing `report`, `report:null`, `"yes"`, `123`, `[]`, `granted` as a string, `policy` as a number, and a report missing required fields — **all** return `caps()=Ok(<verbatim value>)` while the oracle rejects every one with "host returned a malformed capability report"

PROBE PASS (release build, laptop).

## Why it matters

`update_caps` is an admin mutation: it grants/revokes what a world program may use. Today a host (buggy, older, or hostile) that answers `{"type":"caps"}` with a missing/garbled report gets a success exit and a printed `null` instead of an error — the operator believes the capability change took effect and has no report to check it against. The query path has the same hole in the profile output. This is the same silent-default family as #6620 (compile) and #6621 (read_worlds), in a distinct method pair with a mutation on one side.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorldClient::caps` and `WorldClient::update_caps` reject a `caps` reply whose `report` is missing or does not deserialize as `CapsReport`, with an error in the existing style (e.g. "host returned a malformed capability report" / "host sent a malformed capability report")
- [ ] Well-formed reports — including pre-ceiling reports that rely on the `#[serde(default)]` fields (cf. the existing old-report test at `world_net.rs:2621`) — still return Ok and round-trip unchanged for existing `Value` consumers
- [ ] A regression test feeds both methods (or their shared extraction) the malformed shapes above and asserts Err; the refusal-reply path still surfaces the host's message
- [ ] `cargo test -p id world_net` (laptop or CI) green, including the existing caps-over-iroh tests

Distinct from: #6620 (compile reply), #6621 (read_worlds reply), #6600/#6578 (paging cursors). The typed server side is `ServerFrame::Caps { report }` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs:396`); only the client extraction is unchecked.

items.title: id(world): current_world_state parses the whole execution_profile frame as a WorldExecutionProfile — the profile is nested at update.requested, so diff/apply always read the live profile as default and set_profile never converges

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

items.body:
## Bug

`id world diff` and `id world apply` always read the world's execution profile as the all-default profile, no matter what profile the host has actually persisted. Manifest reconciliation therefore never converges for any world/manifest pair that uses a non-default `[profile]`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ de90338c42)

- The host answers `execution_profile_info` / `set_execution_profile` with `ServerFrame::ExecutionProfile { update: ExecutionProfileUpdate { requested, applies_on_next_program_install_or_process_restart }, message }` — the profile is nested at `update.requested` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs:399-402`, `pkgs/id/src/world/mod.rs:1848-1853`, reply built in `pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs`, `ExecutionProfileInfo` arm).
- `WorldClient::execution_profile` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:1029-1059`) returns the **whole reply frame** after only a `type` check — unlike `caps()` (`world_net.rs:791`), which extracts `reply["report"]`.
- `current_world_state` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:1122-1129`) then runs `serde_json::from_value::<WorldExecutionProfile>(whole_frame)` with the context `"host returned a malformed execution profile"`. But `WorldExecutionProfile` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_limits.rs:283-309`) is `#[serde(default)]` with all-`Option` fields and no `deny_unknown_fields`, so parsing **any** object frame succeeds and yields the all-`None` default: the frame's real profile sits under the unknown key `update` and is ignored. The malformed-profile error can never fire for an object reply.
- Consequence in the planner (`pkgs/id/src/world_manifest.rs:340`): a step is planned when `desired.profile != default && desired.profile != current.profile`. Since `current.profile` is always the default, every manifest with a non-default `[profile]` plans a `set_profile` step on **every** diff/apply — including immediately after a successful apply set exactly that profile. `id world diff` reports profile drift forever; apply never reaches "no drift".

## Reproduction (probe, laptop)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-exec-profile-frame` (verbatim copy of the `WorldExecutionProfile` type from `world_limits.rs:283-309`, exact client expression from `commands/world.rs:1122-1129`), run on the laptop this run:

- Host frame for a world with persisted `wasm_fuel=1000000, total_memory_bytes=268435456` → client parse returns `WorldExecutionProfile { all fields None }` (== default). **BUG CONFIRMED.**
- Oracle parse of `frame["update"]["requested"]` → `wasm_fuel: Some(1000000), total_memory_bytes: Some(268435456)`.
- Plan rule (`world_manifest.rs:340`) with desired=oracle, current=parsed → `SetProfile` planned on every diff/apply.

## Why it matters

Manifest diff/apply is the declarative path for world configuration (#838/#807 family). A profile read that is silently always-default makes drift detection meaningless for the profile dimension: perpetual false drift for profile users, re-applies on every run, and no way to notice a host whose persisted profile was changed out-of-band to something the manifest does not want (any actual profile reads as default). The dead `"host returned a malformed execution profile"` error string shows the strictness was intended — the frame shape just never matched the parse.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorldClient::execution_profile` (or `current_world_state`) extracts the profile from `update.requested` (mirroring how `caps()` extracts `report`), so a host-persisted non-default profile reads back identically.
- [ ] A reply whose `update.requested` is missing or mistyped fails with the existing "host returned a malformed execution profile" context instead of reading as the default profile.
- [ ] Regression test: a scripted/frame-level test where the host's persisted profile is non-default and `current_world_state` (or its extraction helper) returns that profile; and a manifest whose `[profile]` equals the live profile plans zero steps / diffs clean after apply.
- [ ] `set_execution_profile`'s return path checked for the same shape assumption and covered by the same extraction, if it shares the consumer pattern.

Related (same client, different fields/functions — not this issue): #6624 (caps report), #6625 (policy reply), #6626 (manifest_state seed).

## Unowned PR batch — branch disposition execution, 2026-11-07

Drew's ruling (2026-11-07 21:53 CST): on the laptop, uncommitted or ahead branches get committed and pushed, then clean local branches fully in origin get deleted; in origin, behind-only branches and merged-PR heads get deleted; branches ahead with real changes (not just merge commits) get a PR each. This issue owns the resulting unowned PR batch.

Triage: ONE triage task per repo on its pilot queue (repo-health-code-pilot / repo-health-opencode-pilot / repo-health-openchamber-pilot / repo-health-nix-pilot) covers that repo's list below. Per PR: validate the work is real and current; outcome is either close the PR with reason or route it to impl/finish/merge as a follow-on fix task.
